question: Can the three measured acquisition failures (sticky ambiguity dead-end, natural false gestures, unstable post-lock following) be fixed by logic changes, measured BEFORE touching the shipped Swift?

variants.hysteresis: post-lock follower: incumbent within 0.12 of anchor keeps identity unless challenger beats its score by ~1.43x (playerTracker gate applied to the live follower)
variants.ambiguity-timeout: sticky ambiguity falls back after 3s to locking the occupant closest to the region center
variants.sustained-gesture: gesture requires 5 consecutive elevated frames (~165ms@30fps) instead of 1

findings: On the 288-case Tier-C aggregate the combined candidate dominates shipped: lock 0.729→0.969, false gesture locks 37→9 (−76%), ≥90%-stable locks 59→90 (+53%), mean on-target 0.493→0.554, correctness 0.700→0.731.

On the 7 verified cases the picture is NOT confirmatory: timeout locks the 3 previously-dead crowd cases but 2 lock the wrong person (correct 5/7), and mean on-target drops because the newly locked crowd cases are the hardest to follow.

Hysteresis improves following in aggregate (+0.05 on-target over 210 locks) but reads slightly worse on the 4 verified locks — n far too small to decide; this is exactly the small-n instability the learning-curve harness quantifies.
decision: DO NOT port to Swift yet. The candidate is promising on aggregate; the verified set (n=7) is too small to confirm and shows a correctness regression risk in crowd fallback locks. Next: verify ≥30 TA cases (queue exists), re-run all variants, then decide. The bench makes that decision a 5-minute measurement.
artifacts: datasets/ta-bench/results/ (5 runs, one per variant), packages/swing-lab/src/engine/taReplay.ts (ReplayVariant)
caveats: Tier-C aggregate uses machine-proposed regions/true-targets (unverified); systematic proposal bias is possible.
Timeout fallback 'closest occupant' can systematically pick a bystander standing dead-center in a contested region — measured as the 2 wrong verified locks.
